_comment: Anthropic effort arm 'high' for Day-to-Day Bench task set v1. Same tasks, graders, output limits (4,096 tokens, reasoning included), judges and repeats as run-config.json; the only change is reasoning_effort high on the three Anthropic models (Anthropic's effort page lists all five levels for Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5, read 17 November 2026). Results are a separate, labelled run and are never merged with the low-effort main result. caps_usd are the provider ledgers' lifetime ceilings: OpenAI 115 as in the OpenAI arms (it pays for the gpt-6.1-terra judge), Anthropic 60 unchanged. Must run before 20 November 2026, when the OpenAI credit that pays the judge expires. At this effort more answers may hit the 4,096-token limit; truncation is graded as it stands and reported per model.
approved_by: Kol (repo owner): typed go for the paid runs in the AI Resource Hub session on 15 November 2026; funded by prepaid API credit (amount private).

canary._comment: Second canary, 15 November 2026. The first (run 2026-11-15T031058Z-aa0ee142) took the default two tasks, both short and script-graded, so it proved the transport and the charges and nothing else. These two exercise what it missed: f5-pub-03 has five judged checks and a long prompt, f7-pub-05 is graded by tests in the sandbox.

_judge_candidates_comment: The qualify stage tries every candidate against the frozen samples, cheapest first, and names the panel: on each side the cheapest candidate that passed. Then set judges to that panel. A judge verdict is a small JSON object, so every judge and candidate has an output limit of 400 tokens.
